extracted.intended_audience: general public; journalists and global citizens concerned about misinformation
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on how journalists and citizens should evaluate information sources, prioritize evidence, and uphold journalistic objectivity in the era of fake news. Emphasizes civic responsibility to understand science and empirical facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be careful where you get information from
rubrics_metrics.description: Be careful where you get information from.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amanpour warns consumers to be selective about information sources to avoid misinformation; included in the talk's central admonition about navigating the era of fake news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appreciate the truth; understand science, empirical evidence and facts
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless we are all engaged as global citizens who appreciate the truth, who understand science, empirical evidence and facts, then we are going to be wandering around -- to a potential catastrophe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize evidence-based reporting and information; evaluate claims by their empirical support and alignment with scientific consensus to guard against falsehoods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectivity in journalism
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amanpour discusses objectivity as a quality journalists should maintain; implies standards of impartial reporting, critical inquiry, and separation of fact from opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage as global citizens
rubrics_metrics.description: We are all engaged as global citizens who appreciate the truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages a civic-duty perspective: individuals should actively seek accurate information and participate in public life with an informed, truth-valuing mindset to prevent societal harm.
